title: GENTILES: NORTHERN KINGDOM IN THE NEW TESTAMENT

sense.text:
“In the twelfth year of Ahaz king of Judah began Hoshea the son of Elah to reign in Samaria over Israel nine years.” While Ahaz ruled over Judah, the northern kingdom had its own king, Hoshea. This is the most pivotal point in time for the northern kingdom: the time it was overthrown.

The kingdom split in the days of Solomon’s son, who was foolish and listened to the friends he grew up with. Judah, made up of three tribes, Judah, Benjamin and Levi, is the southern kingdom. Ephraim and the rest, Manasseh, Simeon, Zebulun, Gad, Reuben, Asher, Naphtali, with Dan, is the northern kingdom. Judah took Rehoboam for their king and Ephraim took Jeroboam.

Those who teach in the street need to acquaint themselves with this history, because the apologists of the Christianity cult out there are retards, retards that cause a lot of confusion: very, very slow in the brain, and may have been dropped multiple times on their heads as children. They concede that we are Israelites; their biggest argument is the Gentiles, that the Gentiles are granted salvation along with the children of Israel. And many of our own people, Coons and sellouts, side with them on this mission of saving everybody, which is insanity and goes back to the slave mentality. Christianity puts white guilt and white fragility into the black man’s mind, and makes black folks step in front of the white man and fight against their own people for his salvation.

They also say Christianity is not a white man’s doctrine because it was taught in Africa, and they run to Tertullian and Augustine, the two black men they can’t argue are black. But the doctrine Tertullian pushed in Africa carried remnants of Western, pagan Christianity. By the time John the disciple died, and his disciple Polycarp, and Irenaeus, the Christian doctrine became degenerate: Jewish folklore and pagan doctrine merged together, and by the second and third century Christianity was finished. That is the Christianity these apologists uphold today, and it started with Rome, which our people ruled over, and they were Coons as well.

“Against him came up Shalmaneser king of Assyria”: Shalmaneser the fifth, king over the Assyrian Empire, the Assyrians with two s’s, not Syria like today. “Hoshea became his servant, and gave him presents”: the king of the northern kingdom became his tributary and paid him taxes.

Then Hoshea “had sent messengers to So king of Egypt”. The northern kingdom tried to ally themselves with Egypt and turn their back on Assyria, so when the Assyrian king got word of the conspiracy, he “shut him up, and bound him in prison.”

He “went up to Samaria, and besieged it three years.” Samaria is the capital of Ephraim.

Then he “carried Israel away into Assyria, and placed them in Halah and in Habor by the river of Gozan, and in the cities of the Medes”: areas of Iran, leading into areas close to Russia. From there the northern kingdom eventually made their way even further, and the bulk of us made our way to the Americas.

It was done in waves. Before Shalmaneser, his father or grandfather, Tiglath-pileser, King Pul, also came against us and took us captive to these same areas. This was one of the last waves of the northern kingdom being taken into exile.

Why it happened: “the children of Israel had sinned against the Lord their God, which had brought them up out of the land of Egypt”, and “had feared other gods, And walked in the statutes of the heathen”, and “did secretly those things that were not right”.

“Therefore the Lord was very angry with Israel, and removed them out of his sight”. This is not the whole nation yet; this is the northern kingdom, removed into the cities of the Medes by Shalmaneser the fifth. “There was none left but the tribe of Judah only”: the southern kingdom, because Judah was the leading tribe over the southern kingdom with Benjamin and Levi.

“Also Judah kept not the commandments of the Lord their God, but walked in the statutes of Israel which they made.” Judah started going off as well, falling in behind the example of the northern kingdom.
“The Lord rejected all the seed of Israel, and afflicted them, and delivered them into the hand of spoilers, until he had cast them out of his sight”: the northern kingdom.

“For he rent Israel from the house of David”. Solomon sinned against the Lord in his idolatry, and the prophet was sent to tell him the kingdom would be ripped in half from his lineage. In the time of Solomon’s son Rehoboam the twelve tribes were ripped in half, so that one king reigned over nine and one king reigned over three.

“They made Jeroboam the son of Nebat king: and Jeroboam drave Israel from following the Lord, and made them sin a great sin”, into idolatry. Jeroboam was the first king over the northern kingdom at the split, and Rehoboam the first king over the southern kingdom. This is emphasized because it is very important.

“So was Israel carried away out of their own land to Assyria unto this day.” The Assyrian policy was that when they conquered you, they displaced you: deport you from your land and place you in foreign lands, so that you lose all sense of nationality, of who you are, where you are from, who your people are, and your God. Living in those foreign lands, a people begin to assimilate and integrate into the heathen society they are placed in. That is what happened to us here: we were removed from our land and placed in others.

The history bears it out. Under the Assyrians the whole area became a vast experiment of cultural mixing, all nations mixed together in one place. Sargon II (721 to 705 BC) forcefully relocated Hebrews after the conquest of the northern kingdom: Shalmaneser deported most of us and Sargon finished the job. It marks the beginning of the scattering of the Israelites. The Hebrews deported from Israel blended in with Assyrian society, behaving like them, following their customs, calling themselves Assyrians, and by the time Nebuchadnezzar conquered Judah they had disappeared, nameless and faceless. You would not know who they were, because they intermingled with the nations. So if the northern kingdom became nameless and faceless, what were they called in the New Testament? Keep the history in mind.

The European borrowed from the ancient Babylonian civilizations and succeeded where they failed. America is an amalgamation of every captivity we have been under, from Egypt all the way to Rome. We are reliving all the captivities at one time, which is why it is the worst and the last, and why we are still destroyed here.

“The king of Assyria brought men from Babylon, and from Cuthah, and from Ava, and from Hamath, and from Sepharvaim, and placed them in the cities of Samaria instead of the children of Israel”. Assyria conquered the northern kingdom, took us out of our land and put us in foreign lands, and put heathens in the land in our stead: “they possessed Samaria, and dwelt in the cities thereof.”

“They feared not the Lord: therefore the Lord sent lions among them”. They were doing disgusting things in our land, and God said they were taking it too far. So the king of Assyria commanded, “Carry thither one of the priests whom ye brought from thence”: bring back a priest of the northern kingdom to teach these nations how to live in the land without being attacked, while they still served their own gods.

“One of the priests whom they had carried away from Samaria came and dwelt in Beth–el, and taught them how they should fear the Lord.” One priest of the northern kingdom was brought back, and he dwelt in Bethel.

“Howbeit every nation made gods of their own”. Despite living in our holy land, these nations did not become us. They remained themselves: they worshipped their own gods, and gave honor to our God only because they had to in order to remain in the land.

They put their gods “in the houses of the high places which the Samaritans had made”. The Samaritans are the northern kingdom of Israel. The Samaritans were never referred to as other nations; the Samaritans were always our people, and that is what they were called in the Old Testament and the New.

“The high places of Isaac shall be desolate, and the sanctuaries of Israel shall be laid waste”. The high places of Isaac here are the northern kingdom, and they would be laid waste because the Assyrians were going to come in and destroy. Amos prophesied in the time of the kings, before Assyria came up and overthrew them; he is prophesying what eventually happened in 2 Kings 17.

“I will rise against the house of Jeroboam with the sword.” The house of Jeroboam is the northern kingdom, the same as the places of Isaac, and the sword is the Assyrian sword.

“Amaziah the priest of Beth–el”. Remember the nations said bring back a priest who can teach us how to live in the land; here is one of the priests of Bethel. Amaziah was a pagan priest of the northern kingdom, and he sent to the king to get the prophet Amos out of there: “the land is not able to bear all his words.” The northern kingdom was tired of hearing him.

“Jeroboam shall die by the sword, and Israel shall surely be led away captive out of their own land.” Amos is prophesying against the northern kingdom, and Hosea was doing the exact same thing at the exact same time. The northern kingdom was not listening.

“O thou seer, go, flee thee away into the land of Judah, and there eat bread, and prophesy there”: get out of here, go teach Judah, leave us alone, we don’t want to hear your prophecy no more. That is how people are today: go teach them Negroes, we don’t want to hear you talking to us about the prophecy against us.

“But prophesy not again any more at Beth–el: for it is the king’s chapel, and it is the king’s court.” Don’t teach the northern kingdom no more; the king is good over here.

“I was no prophet, neither was I a prophet’s son”: Amos did not come from a line of prophets. “I was an herdman, and a gatherer of sycomore fruit: And the Lord took me as I followed the flock, and the Lord said unto me, Go, prophesy unto my people Israel”: prophesy to the northern kingdom.

“Thou sayest, Prophesy not against Israel, and drop not thy word against the house of Isaac.” The house of Isaac here is the northern kingdom. You tell me not to teach you no more and to leave you alone.

“Thy wife shall be an harlot in the city”, because the Assyrians were going to come in there and rape them. “Thy sons and thy daughters shall fall by the sword”: killed. “Thy land shall be divided by line”, and heathen placed in the land, as read in 2 Kings 17. “Thou shalt die in a polluted land”: placed in the cities of the Medes. “Israel shall surely go into captivity forth of his land.”

This is Amos prophesying against the northern kingdom before Shalmaneser and before Sargon.

“In the year that Tartan came unto Ashdod, (when Sargon the king of Assyria sent him,)”. Tartan was a general of Sargon. Sargon was of the same royal line as Shalmaneser (some say brother, some say cousin), and Sargon was the final blow against the northern kingdom: he completed what Shalmaneser left off.

Pul, Tiglath-pileser, came first and took a wave of us away. Then Shalmaneser came and took the bulk, the majority of us, and Sargon took away the remainder of that bulk. But there was a remnant left.

“Therefore will I do unto this house, which is called by my name, wherein ye trust, and unto the place which I gave to you and to your fathers, as I have done to Shiloh.” This is the Lord prophesying against the southern kingdom. Judah followed behind Ephraim into idolatry, so the Lord said, what I did to the northern kingdom I am going to do to you. This place is Judea, and Shiloh was the northern kingdom’s capital, the first place of worship.

“I will cast you out of my sight, as I have cast out all your brethren, even the whole seed of Ephraim.” He will cast Judah, the southern kingdom, out of his sight, as he cast out their brethren, the northern kingdom.

The Lord sent Nebuchadnezzar and the Babylonians against the southern kingdom, and he did the exact same thing Shalmaneser did to the northern kingdom: but Nebuchadnezzar left behind a remnant of the southern kingdom, the poor, in the land. In the same way, the Assyrian king left behind a remnant of the northern kingdom in their land. The same thing happened to both kingdoms by different nations: the Assyrians conquered the northern kingdom, the Babylonians conquered the southern kingdom, and both left remnants in the land.

“So he went and took Gomer the daughter of Diblaim; which conceived, and bare him a son.” The history said Ephraim became nameless and faceless. Once the northern kingdom was overthrown by Assyria, history recognized them as the Lost Tribes of Israel. The bulk of Judah returned after Babylon was overthrown by the Persians, but the northern kingdom remained scattered, and the bulk of them came to this side of the world.

Hosea’s children were signs of prophecy against the northern kingdom and what would happen to them. Amos and Hosea prophesied against the northern kingdom at the exact same time, and Ephraim was still not listening.
“I will break the bow of Israel in the valley of Jezreel.” The first son was named Jezreel: the Lord was going to break Ephraim through Assyria.

“Call her name Lo–ruhamah: for I will no more have mercy upon the house of Israel”. Lo means no, ruhamah mercy: no mercy. The house of Israel here is the northern kingdom. “But I will utterly take them away”: by the Assyrian Empire, as in 2 Kings 17.

“But I will have mercy upon the house of Judah”, because the house of Judah returned to the land. “and will save them by the Lord their God, and will not save them by bow, nor by sword”: God himself would defend Judah.

When Lo-ruhamah was weaned, about three or four years old, she bare another son. “Call his name Lo–ammi: for ye are not my people, and I will not be your God.” Nameless and faceless.

If you are not his people and he is not your God, what are you? Gentiles: strangers, foreigners, aliens.

“Yet the number of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea, which cannot be measured nor numbered”. Despite that, Israel would be as the sand of the sea. “In the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people, there it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living God”, because they will be granted repentance.

“Then shall the children of Judah and the children of Israel be gathered together”. They split into two kingdoms, and prophetically they will be reunited as one. “And appoint themselves one head”: keep this in mind, that one head is Christ, the black Messiah.

“They shall come up out of the land”: land, singular, because the bulk of both kingdoms are in one particular land, America, Babylon the great. The majority of both the southern and northern kingdom were brought here to the Americas, where the northern kingdom was already, as the so-called Native Americans. “For great shall be the day of Jezreel”: they get deliverance together, which is why it is a great day.

“Now in the first year of Cyrus king of Persia”. The Medo-Persian Empire conquered Babylon. Assyria is gone, Babylon is gone: Assyria conquered the northern kingdom, Babylon conquered the southern kingdom, and now Persia is in power under Cyrus. “The Lord stirred up the spirit of Cyrus king of Persia, that he made a proclamation throughout all his kingdom”.

“He hath charged me to build him an house at Jerusalem, which is in Judah.” The Lord moved the spirit of Cyrus to let Israel return to the land and rebuild what Babylon destroyed, for Babylon had destroyed the temple and burnt down our homes. Cyrus gave us the liberty to return from the lands of exile and captivity and rebuild our homeland.

At this point in time both the southern and northern kingdom had the freedom to return home. “Who is there among you of all his people? his God be with him, and let him go up to Jerusalem”: return home and rebuild the house of the Lord, the second temple.

“And whosoever remaineth in any place where he sojourneth”: whoever chooses to stay in the lands where they were scattered, of both kingdoms. If you made a life there, have family there, and are content and complacent, fine: “let the men of his place help him with silver, and with gold, and with goods, and with beasts”. Send funds, by law, to support your brothers who choose to return home and rebuild the homeland you chose not to return to.

“Then rose up the chief of the fathers of Judah and Benjamin, and the priests, and the Levites, with all them whose spirit God had raised”. Judah, Benjamin and Levi, and “with all them” is the remnant of the northern kingdom.

Some argue that all the northern kingdom was taken into captivity and none of them were in the land. That is heresy.

The two kings who conquered the northern kingdom completely, Shalmaneser and Sargon, put an end to the northern kingdom as a state around 722 to 721 BC.

“Began Azariah son of Amaziah king of Judah to reign.” This Azariah in 2 Kings 15 is Uzziah in Chronicles: “Sixteen years old was he when he began to reign, and he reigned two and fifty years in Jerusalem.” It is the same king and the same history. Uzziah is the grandfather or great-grandfather of the righteous king Hezekiah, who reigned after them.

precepts.why: “Then all the people of Judah took Uzziah, who was sixteen years old, and made him king in the room of his father Amaziah.” Kings says Azariah son of Amaziah was sixteen when he began to reign; Chronicles says Uzziah was sixteen, made king in the room of his father Amaziah. The exact same thing: Azariah’s name is Azariah in Kings and Uzziah in Chronicles.

sense.text:
This is the righteous king Hezekiah. He began to reign about 715 or 716 BC: after the reigns of both Shalmaneser and Sargon. Hezekiah was king over Judah, yet he sends to Israel: “Ye children of Israel, turn again unto the Lord God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, and he will return to the remnant of you, that are escaped out of the hand of the kings of Assyria.”

The remnant of you: this is after Sargon and after Shalmaneser. The kings of Assyria did not get all of them.

“Be not ye like your fathers, and like your brethren, which trespassed against the Lord God of their fathers, who therefore gave them up to desolation, as ye see.” The land was desolate for the most part, because most of the northern kingdom was displaced out of the land, but remnants remained, as with the southern kingdom.

Hezekiah sent letters to the northern kingdom to come and keep the passover with him: “the posts passed from city to city through the country of Ephraim and Manasseh even unto Zebulun”. This is after Sargon. If they were all displaced out of the land, why send letters there? Because they were not all out of the land. There were remnants who escaped the onslaught of both Shalmaneser and Sargon; there were Samaritans left.

Keep Zebulun in mind. “But they laughed them to scorn, and mocked them.”
“Nevertheless divers of Asher and Manasseh and of Zebulun humbled themselves, and came to Jerusalem.”

“They killed the passover on the fourteenth day of the second month”, and “there were many in the congregation that were not sanctified”, not purified for the feast, so “the Levites had the charge of the killing of the passovers for every one that was not clean, to sanctify them unto the Lord.”

“For a multitude of the people, even many of Ephraim, and Manasseh, Issachar, and Zebulun”. Some of them mocked, but not all of them: many of Ephraim, Manasseh, Issachar and Zebulun showed up. They “had not cleansed themselves”, because they were out there in idolatry, “yet did they eat the passover otherwise than it was written.”

“But Hezekiah prayed for them, saying, The good Lord pardon every one That prepareth his heart to seek God”. Every one here is the same people as all them of Ezra 1:5, the same group. “Though he be not cleansed according to the purification of the sanctuary”: baptized, the same thing.

“The Lord hearkened to Hezekiah, and healed the people.” “The children of Israel that were present at Jerusalem” were the southern kingdom and the remnant of the northern kingdom, and they kept the feast seven days with great gladness. The remnants of the northern kingdom would always humble themselves and come to honor the Lord.

Another example, from the time of Asa, Hezekiah’s forefather. Asa was a king righteous for a time. “The Lord is with you, while ye be with him; and if ye seek him, he will be found of you; but if ye forsake him, he will forsake you.”

“Now for a long season Israel hath been without the true God, and without a teaching priest, and without law.” Israel here is the northern kingdom. They were without a teaching priest because they kicked the Levites out of their coasts and put dumb idiots there instead, like Amaziah of Bethel. Keep in mind: without their true God, without a teaching priest, without law.
“But when they in their trouble did turn unto the Lord God of Israel, and sought him, he was found of them.”

“He gathered all Judah and Benjamin, and the strangers with them out of Ephraim and Manasseh, and out of Simeon”. Ephraim is called strangers: nameless and faceless, not my people, and not your God. “For they fell to him out of Israel in abundance, when they saw that the Lord his God was with him.”

When God was with Judah, the Lord would humble Ephraim to return to him. Whenever Judah had a righteous king, Ephraim would humble themselves and reunite with the righteous of the southern kingdom, every time. Even in these days the righteous of the southern kingdom are slowly bringing the northern kingdom into the fold, because the righteous of Judah are in the midst. The spirit of the southern kingdom has to be the catalyst to ignite that fire in the northern kingdom: the captains go out where Ephraim is and humble them to bring them back to the Lord. Judah first. That is always the order.

“Those are the ten tribes, which were carried away prisoners out of their own land in the time of Osea the king, whom Salmanasar the king of Assyria led away captive”. This is the history of 2 Kings 17: Hoshea the king, and Shalmaneser. Shalmaneser and Sargon were the final blow against the northern kingdom, but a remnant escaped those kings, and Hezekiah wrote to them to return and keep the passover.

“But they took this counsel among themselves, that they would leave the multitude of the heathen, and go forth into a further country”. When were they allowed to take this counsel among themselves? Not in 722 or 721 BC, when they were conquered: they were in chains, and the Assyrians would have killed them. Saying they left for America the same year they were overthrown is a stupid doctrine. It was Persia: Cyrus gave us the liberty to return from the lands of exile and rebuild, in Ezra 1:1-5.

“Where never mankind dwelt”: that is America, which is why it is called the new world. Where Israel was is called the old world. Shem, Ham and Japheth had the old world: Europe, the so-called Middle East, Africa. No son of Noah had America; no man was here at all.

The history proves it. Various coins have been found in the Americas, buried in the tombs of the natives of the land. The coins the Europeans gave the natives are little worn, but those brought by the first settlers from Asia are much more defaced by time, of a very different stamp, and some of them bear the old Persian stamp. They must have been brought by the first settlers, who had communication with the ancient Persians; and the only people who had dealings with the Persians in that remote time were the Phoenicians and the Jews: the northern and the southern kingdom. The northern kingdom brought those coins here when they were granted liberty, under Cyrus, to return and rebuild Jerusalem.

“That they might there keep their statutes, which they never kept in their own land.” And we did for a while, until we went off into eating hearts, idolatry and madness in those temples.

They had the liberty to return to our land and chose not to. The bulk of the northern kingdom chose to come to this side of the world; remnants remained on the other side. The beef they had with Judah was so strong that they said, we ain’t going back to Jerusalem, we are going to go over there and be righteous, because of that division among ourselves.

“They entered into Euphrates by the narrow places of the river. For the most High then shewed signs for them, and held still the flood, till they were passed over.” “For through that country there was a great way to go, namely, of a year and a half: and the same region is called Arsareth”: another land.
“Then dwelt they there until the latter time”. The northern kingdom will dwell in this land, the Americas, until the last days.

Assyria, Babylon, Persia, and now the Greeks. The king is Antiochus Epiphanes, who sent “an old man of Athens to compel the Jews to depart from the laws of their fathers”. This is an attack on Judah, and his goal was “to pollute also the temple in Jerusalem, and to call it the temple of Jupiter Olympius”.

“And that in Garizim, of Jupiter the Defender of strangers, as they did desire that dwelt in the place.” Write this down: Garizim, Shechem, is the northern kingdom’s capital. In this time the northern kingdom were prone to idolatry. Judah didn’t want it; Ephraim did.

“At that time young Antiochus wrote unto Jonathan, saying, I confirm thee in the high priesthood, and appoint thee ruler over the four governments”. Young Antiochus was a later Greek king of the line of the Antiochus read before. The Hasmonean family, Levites, gained power in the time of the Greeks: we fought against the Greeks and gained some independence and sovereignty, and the Greeks gave Jonathan rule over these four governments. Keep this in mind.

precepts.why: “And concerning the three governments that are added to Judea from the country of Samaria, let them be joined with Judea, that they may be reckoned to be under one, nor bound to obey other authority than the high priest’s.” Three of the governments were out of the country of Samaria, the land of the northern kingdom, joined with Judea under the high priest.

“Wherefore we have ratified unto them the borders of Judea”: that is one government. “With the three governments of Apherema and Lydda and Ramathem, that are added unto Judea from the country of Samaria, and all things appertaining unto them”.

So the Greeks gave us back our land: parts of Judea and portions of Samaria, these four areas. The Israelites gained dominion and rulership over portions of Judea and the areas pertaining to Samaria. Judah, the southern kingdom, gained dominion over the realm of both the southern and the northern kingdom’s lands.

sense.text: Isaiah prophesied around the exact same time as Amos and Hosea, against the northern kingdom, and against both. “When at the first he lightly afflicted the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali”: remember Zebulun, the tribe that humbled themselves in the time of Hezekiah’s rule. The landmass of Zebulun and Naphtali was called “Galilee of the nations.”

“The people that walked in darkness have seen a great light”. The people that walked in darkness go back to the tribes in verse 1, Zebulun and Naphtali: the northern kingdom. The great light is Christ. “They that dwell in the land of the shadow of death, upon them hath the light shined”: the light shined upon the northern kingdom. Verses 1 and 2 go together.

“For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given”: that light of verse 2. When it is said that God so loved the world that he gave his only begotten Son, that is Isaiah 9:6 being spoken of. “And the government shall be upon his shoulder: and his name shall be called Wonderful, Counsellor, The mighty God, The everlasting Father, The Prince of Peace.”

“Of the increase of his government and peace there shall be no end”: his government is his people, and he is the Prince of Peace; in his kingdom there will be peace between the two. “Upon the throne of David, and upon his kingdom”: all twelve tribes. “The zeal of the Lord of hosts will perform this.”

“The Lord sent a word into Jacob, and it hath lighted upon Israel.” That word is the same son of verse 6, sent to Israel. The great light of verse 2 lighted upon Israel: Israel as a whole, but the northern kingdom here. The light, the word and the son are all one and the same.

“And all the people shall know, even Ephraim and the inhabitant of Samaria”. Keep this in mind: even Ephraim and the inhabitant of Samaria will encounter that son, that word and that great light.

They “say in the pride and stoutness of heart, The bricks are fallen down, but we will build with hewn stones”. They had their own place of worship, but the Lord wasn’t having it.

“And there was one Anna, a prophetess, the daughter of Phanuel, of the tribe of Aser”. Her father Phanuel was of the tribe of Asher, so she was a child of Asher. They thought the northern tribes were all gone: where are they? She was of that remnant that remained, that humbled themselves, going back to Hezekiah’s time and Asa’s time.
She “departed not from the temple, but served God with fastings and prayers night and day.” She “spake of him to all them that looked for redemption in Jerusalem.”
“And leaving Nazareth, he came and dwelt in Capernaum, which is upon the sea coast, in the borders of Zabulon”: Christ went into the lands of Zebulun and Naphtali.

“That it might be fulfilled which was spoken by Esaias the prophet, saying, The land of Zabulon, and the land of Nephthalim, by the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles; The people which sat in darkness saw great light”. Look at it in Isaiah 9:1-2, and on through verses 6 to 9. When Christ went to these areas he fulfilled that prophecy. In Isaiah it is Galilee of the nations; here it is “Galilee of the Gentiles”: the land of the northern kingdom.

“From that time Jesus began to preach, and to say, Repent”. He “saw two brethren, Simon called Peter, and Andrew his brother”. The disciples lived in that landmass where the northern kingdom once was the majority. The southern kingdom took possession of a lot of those lands, but a remnant of the northern kingdom was still there, like the sister Anna in Luke 2.

“And he must needs go through Samaria. Then cometh he to a city of Samaria, which is called Sychar, near to the parcel of ground that Jacob gave to his son Joseph.” Sychar is the same area as Shechem, and this is Ephraim’s land.
“Now Jacob’s well was there.” Jacob’s well was given to Ephraim.

“How is it that thou, being a Jew, askest drink of me, which am a woman of Samaria? for the Jews have no dealings with the Samaritans.” Christ was of Judah. Why did the Jews have no dealings with the Samaritans? Because the northern kingdom and the southern kingdom were split apart, and the southern kingdom was told to leave Ephraim alone. There was division between them. The Samaritans were the northern kingdom, the inhabitants of Samaria, so she says, you Jews have no dealings with us.

“Art thou greater than our father Jacob, which gave us the well, and drank thereof himself, and his children, and his cattle?” She is saying that she and Christ have the same ancestry: our father Jacob. That makes her an Israelite. Jacob gave the well, the land, to Joseph’s children: she is Ephraim.

Some say she was a heathen lying about her nationality. Christ knew she had five husbands but didn’t know what child she was from? She must have had a Magneto helmet on so he couldn’t read her mind. That is retarded.
“Whosoever drinketh of the water that I shall give him shall never thirst; but the water that I shall give him shall be in him a well of water springing up into everlasting life.”

“Go, call thy husband, and come hither.” “I have no husband.” “Thou hast well said, I have no husband: For thou hast had five husbands; and he whom thou now hast is not thy husband”. The man she was sleeping with was not her husband; she was fornicating. He was telling her, you’re a ho, you’re in some ho activity right now. He knew that, and he knew what child she was from. Those apologists, and Israelites, who say she lied about her nationality are saying her powers blinded the Messiah.
“Sir, I perceive that thou art a prophet.” You must be a prophet of God to know I have had five husbands; nobody else knew that.

“Our fathers worshipped in this mountain”. The land of Ephraim was a place of worship; Jacob worshipped there, and Shiloh was there. Our fathers, yours and mine, worshipped here. “And ye say, that in Jerusalem is the place where men ought to worship.” Why should I worship over there in Jerusalem when I can worship right here?

“The hour cometh, when ye shall neither in this mountain, nor yet at Jerusalem, worship the Father.” Rome would come and destroy both. “Ye worship ye know not what: we know what we worship: for salvation is of the Jews.” Salvation would come from Judah. Whenever there is a righteous Judah, Ephraim humbles themselves and comes right in along with them.
“The true worshippers shall worship the Father in spirit and in truth”: by accepting Christ.

“I know that Messias cometh, which is called Christ”, the anointed. How did she know? Because they read it. “When he is come, he will tell us all things.” She is quoting Deuteronomy 18:18, because she was an Israelite.
“I that speak unto thee am he.” The one of Deuteronomy 18: that is me.

“Many of the Samaritans of that city believed on him for the saying of the woman, which testified, He told me all that ever I did.” “And he abode there two days.” He sat there two days and taught: not heathens, but these Israelites.

precepts.why: “And Jacob came to Shalem, a city of Shechem, which is in the land of Canaan, when he came from Padan–aram; and pitched his tent before the city. And he bought a parcel of a field, where he had spread his tent, at the hand of the children of Hamor, Shechem’s father, for an hundred pieces of money.” Jacob bought that landmass. This is the parcel of ground of John 4:5.

“And Israel said unto Joseph, Behold, I die”, and “Moreover I have given to thee one portion above thy brethren, which I took out of the hand of the Amorite with my sword and with my bow.” It is the same land: the portion Jacob got at Shechem he appointed to Joseph.

“And the bones of Joseph, which the children of Israel brought up out of Egypt, buried they in Shechem, in a parcel of ground which Jacob bought of the sons of Hamor the father of Shechem for an hundred pieces of silver”. That goes back to Genesis 33 and 48. “And it became the inheritance of the children of Joseph.”

So that is the landmass where Christ was in John 4: Sychar is Shechem, near the parcel of ground Jacob gave to Joseph. This is Ephraim’s land.

“I will raise them up a Prophet from among their brethren, like unto thee, and will put my words in his mouth; and he shall speak unto them all that I shall command him. And it shall come to pass, that whosoever will not hearken unto my words which he shall speak in my name, I will require it of him.”

That is what the woman of Samaria is speaking of when she says “he will tell us all things”. She knew the prophecy because she was an Israelite, and Christ answers that he is that Prophet.

sense.text:
“Saul was consenting unto his death.” In the time of Stephen’s death, Saul, who became Paul, consented, and “there was a great persecution against the church which was at Jerusalem; and they were all scattered abroad throughout the regions of Judea and Samaria, except the apostles.” The twelve apostles remained in Jerusalem, but their disciples, the deacons, were scattered throughout Judea and Samaria.

Remember that the Greeks gave the Hasmonean family, the Levites, the four governments: the lands of Judea and cities of Samaria and what pertained to them. Judah, the southern kingdom, gained dominion over the lands of both the southern and northern kingdoms, as in 1 Maccabees 10 and 11.
“Then Philip went down to the city of Samaria, and preached Christ unto them.” Philip preached Christ in Samaria during the persecution.
They “preached the gospel in many villages of the Samaritans.” They taught many villages of the Samaritans. Who in Samaria were they preaching to?

precepts.why:
“Now they which were scattered abroad upon the persecution that arose about Stephen travelled as far as Phenice, and Cyprus, and Antioch, preaching the word to none but unto the Jews only.” Acts 11 rehashes what took place in Acts 8. Those scattered by the persecution preached to none but the Jews only, Judah only.

So who were they preaching to in Samaria in Acts 8? Judah. Judah resided in the lands where the northern kingdom once was, because in the time of the Greeks, as in 1 Maccabees 10 and 11, we gained dominion of those areas, and some of the southern kingdom moved into the areas of the northern kingdom and lived there. The remnant of the northern kingdom was still there too, as John 4 and Anna of Luke 2 show.

sense.text: “Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ, to the strangers scattered throughout Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia”. Galatia is where the book of Galatians was written to. Who are the strangers scattered? Verse 2 says it: the elect.

“Elect according to the foreknowledge of God the Father”. Foreknowledge means the knowledge of God before: who is God’s elect from before? Israel. So the strangers in verse 1 are Israel. “Grace unto you, and peace, be multiplied.”

precepts.why: “For Jacob my servant’s sake, and Israel mine elect”. Israel is God’s elect. So Peter is writing to the strangers of the elect, which is Israel: the strangers scattered abroad are the northern kingdom.

sense.text: It is the same book, written to the same people, the strangers of chapter 1 verse 1. “But ye are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation, a peculiar people”: that is Israel. “That ye should shew forth the praises of him who hath called you out of darkness into his marvellous light”: that is Isaiah 9:1-2, the great light that shined upon Israel, which Christ fulfilled in Matthew 4:13-18.

“Which in time past were not a people, but are now the people of God: which had not obtained mercy, but now have obtained mercy.” Where is that written? Hosea 1:10. These are the strangers of the northern kingdom scattered abroad.

precepts.why: “I will have mercy upon her that had not obtained mercy; and I will say to them which were not my people, Thou art my people”. He is speaking of the northern kingdom, Lo-ruhamah and Lo-ammi, and that is what Peter is quoting in 1 Peter 2:10. Those who had not obtained mercy and were not a people are the northern kingdom.

sense.text: “That he might make known the riches of his glory on the vessels of mercy, which he had afore prepared unto glory”. Afore means before: before time, in the past, he prepared them unto glory. Who did God afore prepare for glory? Israelites.

“Even us, whom he hath called, not of the Jews only, but also of the Gentiles”. Paul is saying even us, the same ones of afore time. Not of the Jews only, not of Judah, the southern kingdom, only, but also of the Gentiles.

What are the Jews called in the Old Testament? Judah: that is what Jews means. And who are the Gentiles in the Old Testament? Ephraim, the northern kingdom. So Jews is Judah and Gentiles is the northern kingdom. If you don’t understand this, the apologists are going to confound you, and you will get hemmed up and destroyed out there.

“As he saith also in Osee, I will call them my people, which were not my people; and her beloved, which was not beloved.” “In the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people; there shall they be called the children of the living God.” Paul is quoting Hosea 1:10-11 regarding both the southern and the northern kingdom, Judah and Ephraim: the Jews of verse 24 are Judah, and the Gentiles of verse 24 are Ephraim, the northern kingdom.

They are called Gentiles here in Romans 9, and they are called strangers in 1 Peter 1.

“Then said the Jews among themselves, Whither will he go, that we shall not find him? will he go unto the dispersed among the Gentiles, and teach the Gentiles?” What are the dispersed? The scattered: Israel scattered among the nations. So the Gentiles here are called the dispersed, the diaspora. Will he go unto the dispersed of Israel and teach the Gentiles?
“I lay down my life for the sheep.”

“And other sheep I have, which are not of this fold”. This fold is the southern kingdom, the Jews, whom he dealt with first. The other sheep are the Gentiles, the northern kingdom. “Them also I must bring, and they shall hear my voice; and there shall be one fold, and one shepherd.” One fold is the whole of Israel, both kingdoms united, and the one shepherd is Christ, who will be the king.
“If we let him thus alone, all men will believe on him: and the Romans shall come and take away both our place and nation.”

Caiaphas, the high priest, said “it is expedient for us, that one man should die for the people, and that the whole nation perish not.” Keep in mind the one fold and one shepherd, and the dispersed among the Gentiles.

“This spake he not of himself: but being high priest that year, he prophesied that Jesus should die for that nation”. That nation is the southern kingdom, Judah. “And not for that nation only, but that also he should gather together in one the children of God that were scattered abroad.” The children of God scattered abroad are the northern kingdom: the strangers scattered of 1 Peter 1:1, gathered together in one.
“Thy name shall not be called any more Jacob, but Israel shall be thy name”.

“I am God Almighty: be fruitful and multiply; a nation and a company of nations shall be of thee”. The way it is written, the nation is the southern kingdom, and the company of nations is the northern kingdom. It was prophesied in Genesis that it would be a nation and a company of nations: the same exact thing as not for that nation only, but those scattered abroad.

“The next sabbath day came almost the whole city together to hear the word of God. But when the Jews saw the multitudes, they were filled with envy, and spake against those things which were spoken by Paul, contradicting and blaspheming.”

“It was necessary that the word of God should first have been spoken to you”: to Judah first. “But seeing ye put it from you, and judge yourselves unworthy of everlasting life, lo, we turn to the Gentiles”: then to the northern kingdom.

precepts.why: “The Lord also shall save the tents of Judah first”. Judah is raised first. “That the glory of the house of David and the glory of the inhabitants of Jerusalem do not magnify themselves against Judah.” That is why in Acts 8 they went to the Jews only, Judah first, and then later on to the woman of Samaria, the northern kingdom. There is an order to things: Judah first, then the northern kingdom.

sense.text: “Go not into the way of the Gentiles, and into any city of the Samaritans enter ye not”. The Gentiles and the Samaritans of verse 5 are the northern kingdom.
“But go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.” In verse 6 it is the southern kingdom, because the commandment was that Judah should be taught first.

“And the house of Jacob shall be a fire, and the house of Joseph a flame, and the house of Esau for stubble”. Joseph is the northern kingdom, so the house of Jacob here is Judah. Together “they shall kindle in them, and devour them; and there shall not be any remaining of the house of Esau; for the Lord hath spoken it.”

“There was a certain man in Cesarea called Cornelius, a centurion of the band called the Italian band”: a Roman centurion, a soldier. Remember Zebulun, who humbled themselves and came to keep the passover in the time of Hezekiah.

Caesarea was originally part of the territory allotted to the tribe of Zebulun when the land was divided among the tribes of Israel. Rome conquered it and named it after the Roman Caesars, and later it became a significant port city. So the land Cornelius was from was the land of Zebulun. That is why, in Matthew 4, the light shone upon Zebulun and Naphtali.

“A devout man, and one that feared God with all his house, which gave much alms to the people, and prayed to God alway.” He feared God, like Anna did.

This is the Gentile here. The disciples taught Judah first, then Ephraim in John 4, then Zebulun, most likely, in Acts 10. The Christians are going to use Cornelius as a heathen Gentile, but he is from Caesarea, Zebulun’s land: the northern kingdom.
